dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3001.text: A hair-guiding comb, now commonly called 篦. Formed from 竹, with 𣬉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3002.text: That with which one propels a boat. Formed from 竹, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3003.text: To winnow. From 竹; 𠀠 depicts the form, with 丌 as its base below. All graphs in the 箕 group contain 箕.

shuowen:3004.text: To toss rice and remove its husks. Formed from 箕, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3005.text: A base beneath, a stand supporting objects. A pictograph. All graphs in the 丌 group contain 丌. Pronounced the same as 箕.

shuowen:3006.text: The ancient herald who used a wooden-clapper bell to record poems and words. Formed from 辵 and 丌, with 丌 also indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 記.

shuowen:3007.text: The books of the Five Emperors. From 冊 above 丌, placing them respectfully on a raised stand. Zhuang Du explains: 典 is a great book.

shuowen:3008.text: The same as 巽. From 丌 and 𩔊. This is the Changes' Xun hexagram: “the eldest daughter” and “wind.”

shuowen:3009.text: To hand and give to one another; a binding placed on a stand. Formed from 丌, with 甶 indicating the sound. [The clause 約在閣上 is uncertain.]

shuowen:3010.text: Complete or provided. Formed from 丌, with 𠨎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3011.text: To set out a sacrifice. From 酋; 酋 is wine, with 丌 beneath it. The Rites has 奠 sacrifices.

shuowen:3012.text: Hands assisting one another. From 𠂇 and 工. All graphs in the 左 group contain 左.

shuowen:3013.text: A second or difference: differing things do not match. From 左 and 𠂹.

shuowen:3014.text: Skillful workmanship and ornament. It depicts a person possessing compass and square. It shares the idea of 巫. All graphs in the 工 group contain 工.

shuowen:3015.text: A rule or model. Formed from 工, with 弋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3016.text: Skill. Formed from 工, with 丂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3017.text: A measuring square. From 工, depicting a hand holding it.

shuowen:3018.text: To display something with the utmost skill. From four 工. All graphs in the 㠭 group contain 㠭. [The action 極巧視之 is uncertain.]

shuowen:3019.text: To stop up. From 㠭 and 廾, blocking within 宀. 㠭 is like 齊, making even.

shuowen:3020.text: An invocator: a woman able to serve the formless and bring spirits down through dance. It depicts a person dancing with two sleeves and shares the idea of 工. Anciently Wu Xian first became a 巫. All graphs in the 巫 group contain 巫.

shuowen:3021.text: One able to serve divine beings with purification and solemnity. A man is called 覡, a woman 巫. From 巫 and 見.

shuowen:3022.text: Delicious or sweet. From 口 containing 一; 一 is the Way. All graphs in the 甘 group contain 甘.

shuowen:3023.text: Sweet. From 甘 and 舌; the tongue knows sweetness.

shuowen:3024.text: Harmony. From 甘 and 麻; 麻 means to harmonize. 甘 also supplies the sound. Read like 函.

shuowen:3025.text: Satiated. From 甘 and 肰.

shuowen:3026.text: Especially peaceful and happy. From 甘 and a matched pair, 匹耦.

shuowen:3027.text: A word or utterance. Formed from 口, with 乙 indicating the sound. It also depicts breath emerging from the mouth. All graphs in the 曰 group contain 曰.

shuowen:3028.text: To announce. Formed from 曰 and 冊, with 冊 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3029.text: What or how. Formed from 曰, with 匃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3030.text: A word emitting breath. From 曰, depicting breath emerging. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Hu, crown prince of Zheng.”

shuowen:3031.text: Once or formerly, 曾. Formed from 曰, with 兓 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Could he not fear the light?”

shuowen:3032.text: Abundant, repeated speech, 沓沓. From 水 and 曰. Liaodong has Ta county.

shuowen:3033.text: The two parties in a lawsuit, situated east of the court. From 㯥, those managing affairs, and 曰.

shuowen:3034.text: The difficulty of drawing out an utterance. It depicts breath emerging with difficulty. All graphs in the 𠄎 category contain 𠄎.

shuowen:3035.text: A sound of alarm. Formed from abbreviated 乃, with 西 indicating the sound. The large-seal form 𠧟 does not abbreviate. Some say 𠧟 means to go. Read like 仍.

shuowen:3036.text: The appearance of breath moving. Formed from 乃, with 𠧪 indicating the sound. Read like 攸.

shuowen:3037.text: Breath seeking to emerge freely but obstructed above by 一. Ancient writing uses 丂 for 亏 and also for 巧. All graphs in the 丂 group contain 丂.

shuowen:3038.text: An urgent utterance. From 丂 and 由. Some say 甹 means chivalrous; the Three Capital Regions call those who care little for wealth 甹.

shuowen:3039.text: A word expressing a wish. Formed from 丂, with 寍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3040.text: Reversed 丂. Read like 呵.

shuowen:3041.text: The quality 𦘫, apparently agreeable or permissible. Formed from 口 and 丂, with 丂 also indicating the sound. All graphs in the 可 group contain 可. [The rare cross-gloss is unresolved.]

shuowen:3042.text: Different or unusual. Another explanation: unpaired. From 大 and 可.

shuowen:3043.text: Permissible or satisfactory. Formed from 可, with 加 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Well it is for the rich.”

shuowen:3044.text: Sound. From two 可. Ancient writing uses it for 謌.

shuowen:3046.text: A pause in speech. From 丂; 八 depicts breath passing beyond 亏. All graphs in the 兮 group contain 兮.

shuowen:3047.text: An exclamation of alarm. Formed from 兮, with 旬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3048.text: Breath or vapor. Formed from 兮, with 義 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3049.text: A remainder of speech. From 兮, depicting sound rising and carrying upward.

shuowen:3050.text: A sound of pain. From 口 above 丂. All graphs in the 号 group contain 号.

shuowen:3051.text: To call. From 号 and 虎.

shuowen:3052.text: The same as 於. It depicts breath spreading out. From 丂 and 一; 一 levels the breath. All graphs in the 亏 group contain 亏. (Clerical writing now changes it to 于.)

shuowen:3053.text: Diminution of breath. Formed from 亏, with 雐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3054.text: The same as 亏, a word of careful deliberation. From 亏 and 宷. The Book of Zhou says: “On the third day, dinghai.”

shuowen:3055.text: Speech of alarm. Formed from 口 and 亏, with 亏 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3056.text: Speech level and freely extended. From 亏 and 八; 八 means dividing. Yuan Li's explanation.

shuowen:3057.text: Delicious. Formed from 甘, with 匕 indicating the sound. All graphs in the 旨 group contain 旨.

shuowen:3058.text: To taste with the mouth. Formed from 旨, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3059.text: Joy. From 壴 and 口. All graphs in the 喜 group contain 喜.

shuowen:3060.text: Pleased. Formed from 心 and 喜, with 喜 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3061.text: Great. Formed from 喜, with 否 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Wu had Grand Steward Pi.”

shuowen:3062.text: Music set out upright and visible above. From 屮 and 豆. All graphs in the 壴 group contain 壴.

shuowen:3063.text: To stand upright. From 壴 and 寸, holding it. Read like 駐.

shuowen:3064.text: The night-watch drum. Formed from 壴, with 蚤 indicating the sound. The Rites: four rounds at dusk are the great drum; three at midnight announce the coming morning; five at daybreak announce daylight. Read like 戚.

shuowen:3065.text: A drum's sound. Formed from 壴, with 彡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3066.text: Beautiful or excellent. Formed from 壴, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3067.text: To expand outward. The sound of the spring equinox: the myriad things break through their skins and shells and emerge, hence called 鼓. From 壴; 支 depicts the hand striking it. The Rites of Zhou has six drums: 靁鼓, eight faces; 靈鼓, six; 路鼓, four; 鼖鼓, 臯鼓 and 晉鼓, each two. All graphs in the 鼓 group contain 鼓.

shuowen:3068.text: A large drum. Formed from 鼓, with 咎 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The great drum cannot prevail.”

shuowen:3069.text: A large drum is called 鼖, eight feet across and two-faced, used for military drumming. Formed from 鼓, with abbreviated 賁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3070.text: A mounted drum. Formed from 鼓, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3071.text: A drum's sound. Formed from 鼓, with 隆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3072.text: A drum's sound. Formed from 鼓, with 𣶒 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The hand drums rumble.”

shuowen:3073.text: A drum's sound. Formed from 鼓, with 堂 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Beat the drum: its booming.”

shuowen:3074.text: A drum's sound. Formed from 鼓, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3075.text: A drum without sound. Formed from 鼓, with 咠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3076.text: The sound of drums. Formed from 鼓, with 缶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3077.text: Music for returning troops and arranging the army. Another explanation: desire; ascent. Formed from 豆, with abbreviated 微 indicating the sound. All graphs in the 豈 group contain 豈.

shuowen:3078.text: Peaceful ease. Formed from 心 and 豈, with 豈 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3079.text: The quality 㡮: music on completing affairs. Formed from 豈, with 幾 indicating the sound. [The rare cross-gloss is unresolved.]

shuowen:3080.text: An ancient vessel for eating meat. From 口; pictographic. All graphs in the 豆 group contain 豆.

shuowen:3081.text: A wooden 豆 vessel is called 梪. From 木 and 豆.

shuowen:3082.text: A ladle or gourd vessel, 蠡. Formed from 豆, with abbreviated 蒸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3083.text: A kind of 豆 vessel. Formed from 豆, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3084.text: The food 豆飴, apparently bean malt-sugar. Formed from 豆, with 夗 indicating the sound. [The gloss is uncertain.]

shuowen:3085.text: A ritual vessel. From 廾 holding meat above 豆. Pronounced the same as 鐙.

shuowen:3086.text: A vessel for performing rites. From 豆; pictographic. All graphs in the 豊 group contain 豊. Pronounced the same as 禮.

shuowen:3087.text: The ordering of ranks. From 豊 and 弟. The Book of Yu says: “Order and distinguish the eastern work.”

shuowen:3088.text: A 豆 vessel filled abundantly. From 豆; pictographic. Another explanation: the district drinking rite has a 豐侯 object. All graphs in the 豐 group contain 豐.

shuowen:3089.text: Beautiful and tall. From 豐; 豐 means great. 盇 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Beautiful and splendid.”

shuowen:3090.text: An ancient earthenware vessel. Formed from 豆, with 虍 indicating the sound. All graphs in the 䖒 group contain 䖒.

shuowen:3091.text: An earthenware cooking pot. Formed from 䖒, with 号 indicating the sound. Read like 鎬.

shuowen:3092.text: A vessel. Formed from 䖒 and 㿾, with 㿾 also indicating the sound. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:3093.text: A tiger's markings. A pictograph. All graphs in the 虍 group contain 虍.

shuowen:3094.text: The 騶虞: a white tiger with black markings, its tail longer than its body. A benevolent beast, eating only naturally dead flesh. Formed from 虍, with 吳 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Ah, the 騶虞!”

shuowen:3095.text: The appearance of a tiger. Formed from 虍, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3096.text: A tiger's gait. Formed from 虍, with 文 indicating the sound. Read like 矜.

shuowen:3097.text: A tiger ungentle and untrustworthy. Formed from 虍, with 且 indicating the sound. Read like 䣜 county.

shuowen:3098.text: A roar or howl. Formed from 虍, with 𠀒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3099.text: Cruelty. From 虍, a tiger's foot turned back to claw a person.

shuowen:3100.text: Tiger markings, 彪. Formed from 虍, with 彬 indicating the sound.
